notes: SR131 OTTO Home (otto.de), scoped to Wohnen (Home/Living) department. Checked and EXCLUDED the generic sortiertnach=neuheiten sort chip that appears on every category listing (e.g. /wohnen/inspiration/?sortiertnach=neuheiten) -- it returns the identical canonical page/title as the unfiltered listing, only reordering the same product population, not a distinct New Arrivals product set (arbitrary-filter/sort exclusion). Checked and EXCLUDED /neuheiten/ (site-wide, not Wohnen-scoped) -- it 302-rewrites to an unscoped, un-branded selektion query (title 'Gefunden auf Otto.de', data-pagecluster=Einstiegsseite, i.e. a generic landing page, not a real product list). FOUND OTTO's genuine content-tag mechanism for new items: thema=thmntag_neuheit (the literal target term 'Neuheit[en]'). Applied at the Wohnen department root and all 4 in-scope sub-departments, this tag is a real, independently-counted product filter (distinct from the sort mode above). 3 of 4 sub-departments (Moebel/Furniture, Dekoration/Decor, Lampen/Lighting) have their own dedicated, SEO-branded, indexed landing pages (own title/og:title naming the department + 'Neuheiten', robots index,follow). The Wohnen-root page and the 4th sub-department (Heimtextilien/Home Textiles) use OTTO's generic un-branded fallback template (title 'Gefunden auf Otto.de', robots noindex,follow) for the identical thema=thmntag_neuheit filter, yet both still render a genuine product-count element via the same data-item-count mechanism used throughout the site -- flagged per brief's 'record but flag if genuinely unsure' guidance rather than silently included or dropped. Cross-check: the 4 branded/flagged department counts (13791+5002+726+10961=30480) sum to within ~10% of the Wohnen-root figure (33714), a much tighter agreement than seen in the parallel Clearance/Restposten check, supporting that these are a real, consistently-scoped New Arrivals population rather than noise.
